title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition–associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type–specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type–enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.

title: Phylogeny explains differences in the crystal structures and chemistry of vertebrate tooth enamel and enameloid
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
A phylogenetically diverse suite of modern tooth enamel/enameloid bioapatite from fishes, mammals, and reptiles from 22 species were chemically and structurally analyzed to establish whether crystal structure and chemistry are phylogenetically correlated. Rietveld refinement analysis of x-ray diffraction data suggests variable crystallographic parameters across vertebrates. Coupled chemical data show correlations between the
                    a
                    -axis of bioapatite and the proportions of sodium substitution for calcium, the introduction of vacancies, and carbonate substituting for phosphate (B-type substitution) or channel anions (A-type substitution). Principal component analysis of all variables suggests that
                    a
                    -axis lengths are highly influenced by the introduction of carbonate in both crystallographic sites. Phylogenetic variations in chemistry and structure of enamel/enameloid crystals show how biomineralization processes have changed through evolutionary time with implications for variation in biomineralization processes across vertebrate lineages. The predominant controls on tooth enamel/enameloid crystal structure are phylogeny rather than primary diet or habitat. Crystal structure variations also influence material properties across organisms, which may control how teeth are fossilized.

title: Postimpact evolution of the South Pole–Aitken basin revealed by Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: South Pole–Aitken (SPA) basin has recorded complex geological histories of the Moon. It is a critical region for solving lunar fundamental questions but remained unexplored until the Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6 missions of China. Their in situ measurements and the Chang’e-6 samples provided the first ground truth for the SPA evolution. On the basis of these constraints, we found that the SPA impact occurred ∼4.34 billion years ago, generating a thick melt sheet that differentiated to form moderately magnesium (Mg)–rich norites. They are exposed at the SPA central peaks and currently investigated by the Chang’e-4 mission in Von Kármán crater, transported by the Finsen impact to the site. Highly Mg-rich materials were found within SPA, likely products of Mg-suite magmatism, including those exposed at the Apollo western peak ring. They were initially excavated by the Apollo impact at ∼4.2 billion years ago and delivered to the Chang’e-6 site by the Chaffee S impact. A series of other events occurred in the SPA basin subsequently (e.g., the Orientale impact ∼3.87 billion years ago); all of them shaped the architecture of the Moon’s largest impact basin.

title: Spatially multiplexed microneedle biosensors for low-abundance protein biomarker monitoring in dermal interstitial fluid
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Microneedle (MN) biosensors offer a minimally invasive approach for molecular analysis of interstitial fluid (ISF), but multiplexed detection of low-abundance protein biomarkers remains limited by poor spatial functionalization and analytical sensitivity. Here, we introduce a high-resolution transfer-printing strategy that functionalizes individual MNs with distinct biorecognition elements on a single patch, enabling simultaneous capture and on-needle analysis of multiple protein biomarkers. Combined with plasmonic-enhanced ultrabright fluorescent nanolabels, the platform enables sensitive multiplexed quantification of low-abundance immune and kidney function biomarkers in mouse models and human subjects. ISF biomarker concentrations showed strong correlations with corresponding plasma levels, supporting the physiological relevance of MN-based measurements. The MN patch enabled painless, blood-free sampling with rapid skin recovery and no irritation. This scalable platform provides a versatile approach for minimally invasive biomarker profiling and may facilitate frequent disease monitoring and timely clinical decision-making.

title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation. We report near-unity efficiency quantum frequency conversion over a bandwidth >45 terahertz, which allowed us to measure the state with an electron-multiplying CCD (EMCCD) camera-based spectrometer, at noncryogenic temperatures. The parametric amplification and conversion of >400 frequency modes yielded an overall mean of ∼700 visible photons per shot and photon statistics consistent with squeezing. Our work shows how many-mode quantum states of light can be generated, manipulated, and measured with efficient use of hardware resources, motivating the use of frequency encoding in quantum optics.

title: Dynein-dependent positioning of multiple organelles regulates adaptive gene expression during oxidative stress
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Cells respond to environmental insults through well-characterized changes to their transcriptome and proteome. The contribution that reorganization of intracellular architecture makes to the adaptive stress response is much less understood. Here, we reveal a conserved spatial response to oxidative stress in which the microtubule motor dynein enhances perinuclear clustering of multiple membrane-bound organelles. These events are triggered by reactive oxygen species and protein kinase C and occur without increased association of dynein with its activator dynactin, pointing to a noncanonical mechanism for stimulating retrograde transport. Using a chemically inducible system for dispersing individual organelles, we show that perinuclear localization of multiple compartments potentiates oxidative stress–induced gene expression, with distinct genes depending on inputs from either combinations of organelles or individual compartments. Together, these findings implicate positioning of multiple membrane-bound compartments in gene expression regulation and identify coordinated organelle trafficking by dynein as an additional regulatory layer in the cellular stress response.

title: Spheroid-laden hydrogels with dual biomimetic intra- and perispheroidal niches for enhanced bone healing
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Stem cell spheroid–hydrogel platforms offer promise for bone defect repair, but implantation-associated oxidative stress, poor vascular ingrowth, and insufficient osteogenic cues limit their clinical translation. Here, we developed dual-NICHE (dual niche-instructive construct for bone healing and engraftment), a gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel containing human adipose–derived stem cell spheroids with spatially distinct intra-/perispheroidal niches. Within a single construct, these two niches provide complementary functions to simultaneously address the key bottlenecks in bone regeneration. The intraspheroidal niche incorporated bone morphogenetic protein-2–immobilized fibers to promote osteogenic differentiation, whereas the perispheroidal matrix contained Sr
                    2+
                    –tannic acid nanoparticles (NPs). Upon implantation, the NPs mitigated oxidative stress and supported vascular infiltration. Concurrently, the osteogenic cue promoted differentiation, while the NPs facilitated mineral nucleation and growth, as further supported by molecular dynamics simulations. Together, this spatial integration enhanced vascularized bone formation with a bone volume fraction of ∼13.5% using only 5208 cells per defect in a mouse calvarial model, providing a potentially translatable framework for bone regeneration.

title: In vivo screening reveals new regulators of natural killer cell development and functional response to acute cytomegalovirus infection
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical innate immune effectors in antiviral and antitumor responses. However, the factors governing NK cell development and function remain incompletely understood. To address this, we adopted an in vivo screening approach, generating a panel of mice deficient in genes differentially expressed across NK cell maturation stages or following viral infection. We performed a combinational screen comprising baseline immunophenotyping and mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) challenge. We identified regulators of NK cell development, including transcriptional regulators and proteins with putative trafficking functions. MCMV challenge studies additionally identified proteins that affected antiviral immunity independently of NK cell phenotypes, including a previously undescribed regulator of NK cell degranulation, synaptotagmin-like protein 3. Identified genes exhibited a trend toward reduced tolerance to loss of function in large-scale human sequencing studies and evidence for reduced NK cell numbers in a cohort of patients with immunodeficiency. Together, these findings provide a resource of NK-expressed genes important for NK cell maturation and function, with relevance to human health.

title: Posttranscriptional regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 controls the transcriptional program enforcing T cell quiescence
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Immune protection against infections relies on long-term maintenance of a highly diversified naïve T cell repertoire. Transcription factors cooperate to enforce T cell metabolic quiescence and maintenance. However, less is known about the posttranscriptional networks that preserve naïve T cells. Here, we describe the RNA binding proteins T cell antigen 1 (TIA1) and TIA-like 1 (TIAL1) as key promoters of CD4 and CD8 T cell quiescence. T cells deficient in TIA1 and TIAL1 undergo premature T cell activation, exhaustion, and death in the absence of cognate antigens. Mechanistically, TIA1 and TIAL1 promote the messenger RNA translation of quiescence-associated transcription factors such as forkhead box P1, lymphoid enhancer factor 1, and T cell factor 1 to restrain homeostatic T cell proliferation and activation. In summary, our study highlights a previously unrecognized dependency on posttranscriptional gene regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 for implementing the quiescent transcriptional programs for long survival of T cells.

title: Engineering interfacial nucleation and growth for long-life, ultrahigh-rate anode-free sodium batteries
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The practical application of anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs) is limited by the poor reversibility of sodium plating and stripping on current collectors. Here, we show that conventional graphite unexpectedly regulates sodium plating and stripping through a dynamic, interactive interface that enables multidimensional charge transport. This behavior arises from the combination of ultrafast mixed ion-electron transport, reversible ether solvent cointercalation, and the anisotropic flake architecture of graphite, which together promote efficient charge exchange and edge-dominant nucleation. The resulting adaptive interface forms an ultrathin, mechanically robust SEI that stabilizes sodium plating and stripping across a wide current density range (1C to 10C). Ampere hour–level anode-free pouch cells based on this design exhibit an initial Coulombic efficiency of 92.3%, retain 84.9% capacity after 1100 cycles at 3C, and display exceptional safety characteristics, including minimal temperature rise at high rates and no thermal runaway during nail penetration. These results establish a platform for controlling interfacial metal nucleation and growth in AFSBs.

title: Pten regulates neurogenic radial glia lineage progression and tunes neocortical astrocyte production in Mapk1/3-dependent pathway
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The cerebral cortex consists of immense numbers of diverse cell types derived from radial glial progenitor (RGP) cells. How RGPs generate appropriate quantities of distinct cell types to safeguard a brain of correct size is not well understood. However, genetic aberrations in human, including mutations in
                    PTEN
                    , lead to cortical malformation such as macrocephaly, albeit with unknown etiology. Here, we used mosaic analysis with double markers (MADM)–based clonal analysis and single-cell phenotyping to decipher the role of
                    Pten
                    in RGP lineage progression during cortical ontogeny. Although neurogenic RGP lineage progression was altered and projection neuron production doubled in the absence of
                    Pten
                    , cortical astrogenesis was drastically increased. Through epistasis experiments, we show that the loss of
                    Pten
                    uncouples astrogenesis from essential growth factor signaling hubs, funneling into MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase). Collectively, our results suggest that
                    Pten
                    regulates RGP lineage progression with distinct sequential functions in corticogenesis to safeguard the emergence of a correctly sized cortex.

title: USP8 inhibition suppresses prostate tumorigenesis via promoting RICTOR degradation to inhibit mTORC2 signaling
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
RICTOR plays an essential role in regulating mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) kinase activity, but it remains largely elusive how RICTOR is aberrantly activated in human prostate cancer (PrCa). Here, we identify RICTOR as a substrate of Cullin 3–based ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP, an important tumor suppressor in PrCa. SPOP deficiency or cancer-derived
                    SPOP
                    mutations disrupt SPOP-mediated degradation of RICTOR, thereby promoting PrCa progression. Furthermore, we identify USP8 as its upstream deubiquitinase, and inhibition of USP8 specifically suppresses RICTOR/mTORC2 activity without affecting mTORC1. As such, the USP8 inhibitor induces RICTOR degradation concomitant with marked tumor suppression in vivo. Hence, these findings reveal an SPOP-USP8-RICTOR regulatory circuit that underlies PrCa tumorigenesis and provides a rationale for targeting RICTOR via USP8 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for patients with PrCa.

title: An ensemble of functionally distinct factors enables spatial quality control during proteasome base assembly
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The proteasome is an essential mediator of the ubiquitin–proteasome system and a complex molecular machine. Hallmarks of de novo proteasome assembly include dedicated chaperones and many subunits, culminating into major assembly intermediates such as the base. Emerging evidence suggests that proteasome assembly is subject to extensive quality control (QC). To understand mechanisms of QC, we examined a crucial assembly checkpoint during base assembly. Our findings reveal sequential mechanisms of QC, in which a checkpoint complex is first assembled, then sequestered into the nucleus, away from ongoing proteasome assembly in the cytoplasm. Assembly of this checkpoint complex depends on noncanonical ubiquitination of the Nas2 chaperone. The Nas2 ubiquitin chain functions as a scaffold by binding the Rpn13 ubiquitin receptor, which is distantly positioned within the same complex. Rpn13 also positions the ubiquitin chain to its neighboring Hul5 ubiquitin ligase, for continual chain elongation to further stabilize this complex. Ubiquitin-mediated assembly enables spatial sequestration of this checkpoint complex through its intrinsic nuclear localization signal (NLS). This NLS on Rpt4 specifically targets this checkpoint complex into the nucleus, emphasizing the importance of spatial compartmentalization. Our findings reveal that proteasome assembly integrates multiple functionally distinct components as QC factors (1 assembly chaperone, 2 ubiquitin regulators, and 1 NLS) to distinguish correct vs. incorrect assembly events en route to a proteasome holoenzyme. These components are not simply passengers in assembly intermediates with their activities reserved for mature proteasomes, but their fundamental functions in cellular proteolysis may begin by first ensuring the accuracy of proteasome assembly.

title: Chromatin loci move coherently due to spatially correlated fluctuations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
From enhancer-promoter communication to DNA repair, essential genome functions require chromosomal loci to encounter each other. While live-cell imaging enables direct measurement of pairwise locus dynamics, a quantitative framework for interpreting them is lacking. Here, using imaging data from
                    Drosophila
                    embryos and mouse stem cells, we show that nearby loci diffuse relative to each other far more slowly than expected from polymer chain–mediated effects. We propose that this slowdown is caused by spatially correlated fluctuations (SCFs) which couple loci via the nucleoplasm. We theoretically predict how these fluctuations scale with space, time, and genomic separation and confirm these predictions using live-cell imaging. Using polymer simulations, we demonstrate that while spatially correlated equilibrium noise fails to reproduce the observed SCF scalings, coupling the polymer to actively driven flows recapitulates the experimental statistics. Consistently, we experimentally show that SCFs couple locus motion across chromosomes and that their magnitude depends on adenosine 5′-triphosphate (ATP)–dependent activity and cohesin-mediated loop extrusion. By reducing encounter frequencies while prolonging encounter durations, SCFs generate a trade-off with direct implications for gene regulation. Our results provide a quantitative framework for chromatin dynamics, revealing how nuclear activity governs chromatin encounters in living cells.

title: ACSS2 modulates endothelial glycolysis in angiogenesis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Endothelial cells (ECs) sustain high glycolytic flux and display remarkable metabolic plasticity. Although molecular pathways regulating endothelial glycolysis are well characterized, metabolic mechanisms underlying hypoxia-induced glycolytic activation during angiogenesis remain poorly understood. Here, we show that acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 (ACSS2) serves as a critical metabolic modulator, coupling acetate utilization with glycolytic flux to control EC function and angiogenesis. The high level of ACSS2-mediated acetate-to-acetyl-CoA conversion in angiogenic front ECs sustains acetyl-CoA levels, which are essential for EC proliferation and retinal vascularization. Conversely, endothelial-specific
                    Acss2
                    deletion disrupts pathological angiogenesis and normalizes tumor vasculature. Mechanistically, ACSS2 maintains hypoxia-inducible factor 1α transcriptional activity and stabilizes glucose transporter 1, thereby preserving glycolysis. Pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 knockdown rescues metabolic and functional defects in ACSS2-deficient ECs, revealing the vital role of acetyl-CoA homeostasis in modulating hypoxic endothelial metabolism. Taken together, these data establish ACSS2 as a pivotal regulator of vascular development and suggest that targeting acetate metabolism may be an effective way to modulate pathological angiogenesis.

title: Four phases and temporal threshold of population calcium response during locomotion in cortical astrocytes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Calcium activity is a major form of astrocyte excitability. Astrocytic calcium events arise spontaneously and in response to behavior, but how unitary events shape population-level activity remains unclear. Using two-photon imaging in the primary somatosensory cortex of awake mice running on a freely rotating disk, we analyzed calcium dynamics during quiescence and locomotion. During quiescence, population fluctuations were driven mainly by the co-occurrence of new events rather than by their enlargement. During locomotion, responses progressed through four phases: emergence of new events, their merging into a superevent, fragmentation, and an afterburst. These responses combined the progressive recruitment of active regions with amplification of a reproducible spatial calcium pattern. New events emerged within the first seconds after locomotion onset, indicating a rapid astrocytic response. A full population response required about 5 s of locomotion: Shorter episodes failed to develop the superevent and produced markedly smaller responses. In suprathreshold episodes, the superevent displayed a reproducible ΔF/F pattern. Hotspots within this pattern had shorter latencies and were also more active during quiescence. A dynamic mode decomposition with control model driven by synthetic or real locomotion inputs reproduced the response phases, temporal threshold, and superevent pattern. These findings show that locomotion-evoked astrocytic calcium activity is an ordered, threshold-dependent population process with reproducible spatiotemporal structure that can be approximated by a low-dimensional dynamical system.

title: Intracellular Bacterial Imprinting Enables Preservable Whole‐Cell Vaccination
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Whole‐tumor‐cell vaccines preserve broad tumor‐antigen repertoires, but converting living tumor cells into safe and intrinsically immunogenic vaccine substrates remains challenging. Here we generated bacteria‐imprinted tumor (BiT) cells through the controlled internalization of attenuated
                    Salmonella
                    and subsequently prepared them as nonproliferative cellular vaccines by freeze‐drying. Within a defined bacterial‐loading window, intracellular
                    Salmonella
                    induced endoplasmic reticulum stress‐associated immunogenic preprogramming while preserving tumor‐cell integrity, thereby enhancing danger‐signal exposure, antigen‐presentation capacity, and immune visibility. Freeze‐drying preserved the bacteria‐induced immunogenic imprint by retaining key molecular and functional attributes while maintaining overall cellular architecture and markedly reducing residual bacterial viability. Vaccination with freeze‐dried BiT (FD‐BiT) cells elicited coordinated innate and adaptive immune responses, including antigen‐presenting cell activation, T follicular helper‐B‐cell cooperation, and germinal‐center formation. This coordinated T–B cell response was accompanied by durable memory formation and enhanced intratumoral CD8
                    +
                    T‐cell infiltration, proliferation, and functional maintenance. Accordingly, FD‐BiT reduced primary tumor establishment and pulmonary metastasis and restrained the growth of tumors that emerged despite prophylactic vaccination. These findings establish intracellular bacterial programming and freeze‐drying‐mediated imprint preservation as a cell‐engineering principle for whole‐tumor‐cell vaccination.

title: Manipulating Monomicelle Monolayer Assembly via Salt Effect Toward Tailorable Mesoporous Polydopamine Superstructures for Aqueous Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The inherent thermodynamic instability of isotropic soft micelles drives their conventional bulk aggregation toward multilayered mesoporous structures, while stabilizing monomicelles and manipulating their monolayer assembly into mesoporous superstructures poses a significant challenge. Here, we report a salt effect‐modulated monomicelle assembly strategy for the precise construction of monolayer mesoporous polydopamine superstructures. The concerted salt effect arising from Debye screening and salting‐out stabilizes the composite monomicelles, reduces their hydrophilicity, and promotes their migration and lateral monolayer assembly at the emulsion interface. Increasing the salt content accelerates assembly kinetics, enhances interfacial affinity, and increases micellar rigidity, enabling tunable interfacial coverage and thereby producing a series of monolayer mesoporous superstructures, including monolayer honeycomb‐like mesoporous nanosheets, monolayer honeycomb‐like mesoporous vesicles, monolayer compound eye‐like mesoporous vesicles, and monolayer compound eye‐like mesoporous nanosheets. As a proof of concept, monolayer honeycomb‐like nanosheets with open mesochannels and abundant functional groups were demonstrated as a nano‐ion divider. By homogenizing the ion flux and enhancing ion affinity and transport, this architecture enables dendrite‐free Sn aqueous batteries with an exceptional lifespan of 2794 h. This work opens new avenues for constructing monolayer superstructures with unparalleled architectural modularization.

title: Modulating Compound Orientations by Modular Synthesis of Lyotropic Liquid Crystalline Alignment Media
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents

ABSTRACT
                  
                    The unambiguous determination of relative configuration is an indispensable part of modern compound development in chemistry and medicine. Anisotropic NMR parameters, like residual dipolar couplings (RDCs), are of global nature providing angular structure information and thus complement established structure elucidation methods. RDCs become accessible if the compound in question is oriented with respect to the magnetic field, for example, by using a lyotropic liquid crystal. Modern approaches of RDC‐based structure elucidation do not rely on a priori models of structure and dynamics but require RDC sets of several linearly independent orientations. Herein, the modular synthesis of a series of substituted polyglutamates, all of which form lyotropic liquid crystals in organic solvents, is presented. The new alignment media become accessible from a time‐efficient and straightforward procedure, additionally giving access to functionalities inaccessible via conventional polypeptide synthesis. The orientation of a model compound is investigated as a function of the different side chain motifs. It is demonstrated that these different side chain motifs are clustered into different categories, with linearly independent orientations provided across these clusters. We demonstrate that data are highly complementary, allowing structure elucidation of a model compound using vector orientations from

The lack of predictive structural descriptors linking molecular precursors with atomic‐scale active‐site evolution limits the rational design of high‐performance M−N−C catalysts. title: Microstructure Engineering of Organic Mixed Ionic‐Electronic Conductors, an Emerging Toolbox for Performance Enhancement and New Applications
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Organic mixed ionic‐electronic conductors (OMIECs) have attracted growing attention for biointegrated electronics and human‐robot interfaces because they can transduce ionic signals into electronic outputs, while offering mechanical compliance for seamless integration with soft biological systems. Achieving high‐performance in OMIEC‐based devices requires precise control over structural parameters across multiple length scales, from molecular‐level chemical structure to macroscopic device architecture. Particularly, because OMIECs operate through direct contact with electrolytes and rely on coupled ionic and electronic transport, microstructural engineering provides a powerful strategy to regulate the electrolyte‐OMIEC interface, ion‐transport pathways, and volumetric doping behavior, thereby bridging molecular design and device‐level architecture. In this review, we categorize microstructural engineering strategies for OMIECs across different length scales, ranging from nanoscale phase‐separated domains to microscale porous and three‐dimensional architectures, and discuss the underlying structure‐formation mechanisms and key processing parameters of each approach. Using organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) as a benchmark platform, we summarize how these strategies have been implemented to enhance device performance and enable new functionalities, while also highlighting their limitations and remaining challenges. Finally, we examine applications of microstructured OMIECs beyond OECTs, focusing on electrochromic devices, and discuss future directions for establishing a deeper understanding of microstructure‐property relationships in mixed ionic‐electronic conducting materials.

title: Stage‐Specific Pressure Programming Decouples Low‐Pressure Sulfur Reduction From High‐Pressure Interfacial Reconstruction in All‐Solid‐State Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The commercialization of all‐solid‐state Li–S batteries (ASSLSBs) remains constrained by the “impossible trinity” between high energy density, long cycle life, and low stack pressure. Here we show that stack pressure is not merely a static mechanical boundary, but a stage‐specific regulator of sulfur conversion and interfacial reconstruction. Using a static pressure‐resistance‐overpotential (P‐R‐η) operational threshold algorithm, low‐stack‐pressure operation is predicted feasible for 50 wt% S cathodes. Further operando electrochemical measurements and multiscale chemical and structural characterizations reveal that 1 MPa discharge promotes Li

State‐resolved very‐small‐angle neutron scattering (VSANS) further uncovers a ∼5 nm structural feature that persists after low‐stack‐pressure discharge, which specifically diminishes upon high‐pressure charging. Guided by this mechanism, we implement a pressure‐programmed protocol combining 1 MPa discharge with 180 MPa charge. The resulting cell retains 98.8% of capacity after 100 cycles at 30 °C. This work establishes a dynamic pressure modulation strategy towards alleviating the “impossible trinity” by decoupling the asymmetric pressure‐electrochemical behaviors.

title: Biomimetic Subcellular Chemomechanical Nano‐Regulator for Allergic Rhinitis Treatment
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a highly prevalent and debilitating chronic inflammatory disease; however, its complex pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely explored, resulting in a significant lack of effective therapeutic strategies in clinical practice. Here, we found that the submucosal extracellular matrix undergoes profound pathological stiffening during AR development and is associated with severe epithelial mechanometabolic dysfunction and physical barrier collapse. Based on this pathomechanical observation, we developed a spatiotemporally programmable subcellular chemomechanical regulator (SCM) to reconstruct the damaged mucosal barrier. Capitalizing on its precise targeting and cascade‐responsive capabilities, SCM provides immediate anti‐inflammatory activity to stabilize stressed epithelial cells. Beyond this acute intervention, the regulator scavenges intracellular free radicals, attenuates pathological mitochondria‐associated membrane (MAM) over‐coupling, and restores mitochondrial metabolic homeostasis. In parallel, the Mn‐containing nanocore and pirfenidone jointly attenuate fibroblast activation and abnormal extracellular‐matrix stiffening. Formulation‐resolved cellular and animal studies distinguished a predominant TA‐associated contribution to early inflammatory and epithelial‐barrier responses from a predominant PFD‐associated contribution to later matrix remodeling. Full SCM combined these stage‐associated response domains while rebuilding epithelial‐barrier integrity and shifting systemic immune readouts toward tolerance. These findings provide a preclinical mechanobiology‐guided framework for treating AR and other mechanically driven inflammatory diseases.

title: In Situ Programming of Armored CAR‐Macrophages by Microneedle‐Mediated Gene Delivery for Melanoma Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Despite clinical advances in CAR‐T therapy and immune checkpoint blockade, effective immunotherapy for solid tumors remains limited by restricted immune‐cell access and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR‐M) provide an alternative strategy by combining antigen‐directed myeloid programming with local immune remodeling. A self‐locking microneedle platform incorporating mannose‐modified nanoparticles (MNPs) enables localized in situ programming of CAR‐expressing macrophages at melanoma sites. The platform co‐delivers a tumor‐antigen‐directed CAR and a hypoxia‐responsive anti‐PD‐L1 single‐chain variable fragment (scPD‐L1). Initial studies in B16F10‐OVA tumors establish antigen‐dependent CAR activity and coordinated local immune remodeling. Therapeutic efficacy is subsequently evaluated in parental B16F10 tumors using an endogenous tyrosinase‐related protein 1 (TYRP1)‐directed CAR. MNP(TYRP1/scPD‐L1) microneedles delay tumor progression, prolong survival, and promote coordinated myeloid and CD8
                    +
                    T‐cell responses, while providing lower terminal tumor burden, greater local surface CAR
                    +
                    tumor‐associated macrophage abundance, and reduced systemic exposure compared with dose‐matched intratumoral administration. Reciprocal depletion further shows that CAR‐programmed macrophages contribute to the antigen‐directed myeloid response, whereas CD8
                    +
                    T cells are major downstream effectors required for maximal and sustained tumor control. These findings establish a localized transcutaneous strategy that coordinates antigen‐directed myeloid programming with adaptive antitumor immunity.

title: Probing Phonon Dynamics for Kinetic Stabilization of Single‐Crystal Nickel‐Rich Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Structural degradation and lattice oxygen loss remain major obstacles to the long‐term stability of nickel‐rich layered cathodes, especially under high‐voltage and high‐rate operation. Conventional strategies primarily rely on thermodynamic stabilization via cation doping or surface protection, while the kinetic dimension of oxygen release has received less attention. Herein, we investigate Si─Ti co‐doped single‐crystal LiNi

Combined Raman spectroscopy and phonon dispersion calculations suggest that Si─Ti co‐doping enhances phonon scattering and modifies TM─O optical phonon modes. Operando and synchrotron‐based characterizations reveal substantially enhanced reversibility of lattice oxygen redox and transition‐metal local coordination. As a result, the optimized cathode exhibits suppressed oxygen release and mitigated irreversible phase transitions, retaining 83.17% of its initial capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 C. These improvements are likely associated with the synergistic effects of thermodynamic and kinetic stabilization, with phonon dynamics proposed as one possible contributor among these coupled effects. This work highlights that the kinetic factors relevant to oxygen release warrant greater attention in the design of durable Ni‐rich cathodes.

ABSTRACT

title: Beyond Lithium Solvation: Tuning Cation‐Solvent‐Anion Interactions for Stable Lithium‐Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Electrolyte chemistry in nonaqueous solvents is central to the electrochemical performance of high‐energy rechargeable batteries, yet the molecular basis of ion solvation in these systems remains incompletely understood. In conventional dipolar aprotic electrolytes, the high electron‐donating ability of the solvent favors cation‐dominated ion‐dipole interactions, such that anions remain largely free or are only weakly incorporated into cation solvation structures. Here we establish an explicit molecular picture of cation‐solvent‐anion ternary interactions in nonaqueous electrolytes and show that these interactions critically govern both bulk electrolyte properties and electrode‐electrolyte interfaces. We find that fluorinated ether‐based solvents, despite being widely regarded as non‐solvating diluents, can exhibit selective solvation of high‐electron‐donating anions, including halides and polysulfides. Coupling these ternary interactions to the redox chemistry of sulfur electrodes suppresses the dissolution and migration of polysulfide intermediates in ether‐based electrolytes, thus mitigating the shuttle effect and improving the cycling stability of Li°||S cells. More broadly, our findings revise the prevailing view of solvation in nonaqueous electrolytes and provide a molecular framework for solvent design and electrolyte formulation to advance high‐energy lithium‐ and other monovalent cation‐based rechargeable batteries.

title: Brønsted Acid Enrichment Around Zeolite‐Encapsulated Pd Promotes Efficient Tandem Catalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Metal‐acid bifunctional catalyst design is essential for selectivity control in tandem catalysis. However, reactive intermediates often experience a kinetic mismatch between metal‐ and acid‐catalyzed elementary steps, thereby being consumed through competing pathways and diverted toward undesired products. Herein, we developed a metal cation‐directed Al siting (MCD‐Al) strategy to enrich framework Al sites around Pd nanoparticles encapsulated in Beta zeolite (Pd@Beta‐MCD), enabling tunable Brønsted acid site density close to metal sites by controlling metal precursor loading. When Pd@Beta‐MCD was employed in benzene hydroalkylation, the spatial proximity of metal–acid sites accelerated transfer of Pd‐generated cyclohexene to adjacent acid sites, and the high Brønsted acid site density around Pd nanoparticles remarkably facilitated cyclohexene protonation for alkylation. Pd@Beta‐MCD achieved its maximum cyclohexylbenzene yield of 48.1% with a corresponding selectivity of 77.5%, outperforming Pd/HBeta (21.1% and 30.1%) and Pd@HBeta (27.7% and 38.3%), representing the best performance reported to date for this reaction. Moreover, Pd@Beta‐MCD showed superior cycling stability over eight runs. We demonstrated that the concentrated Brønsted acid sites adjacent to metal centers resolve the kinetic mismatch and steer the cyclohexene intermediate toward an alkylation‐dominated pathway. This work provides an effective strategy to strengthen metal–acid synergistic matching and facilitates precise control of key intermediates in tandem catalysis.

title: From Empirical Tuning to Predictive Design: Decoupling Dynamic Bottlenecks in Photocatalytic H2O2 Production via Z‐Score Importance Analysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Deconvoluting the intertwined dynamic bottlenecks of photogenerated charge and reaction substrates remains a fundamental bottleneck in heterogeneous photocatalysis due to the lack of reasonable and effective tools. This study presents a quantitative, interpretable framework to deconvolve the entangled factors limiting solar‐driven photocatalysis. Using Au(I)‐based covalent metal‐organic framework (CMOF‐Au) isomers with controlled stacking (AA, AB, and ABC) as a model platform for hydrogen peroxide photosynthesis, we applied a Z‑score and LOFO (Leave‐One‐Feature‐Out) importance analysis. This approach revealed that the dominant rate‐determining factor shifts with stacking: bulk charge transfer governs performance in AA stacking, whereas surface adsorption limits AB and ABC stacking. The method successfully quantifies the relative contribution weights of key functions (charge dynamics, interfacial transfer, surface adsorption, and mass transport) and demonstrates high predictive power across diverse photocatalysts, including covalent organic frameworks, porous aromatic frameworks, C

                    4

By uncovering counterintuitive mechanisms, such as Simpson's paradox, our work establishes a generalizable strategy for decoupling multivariate factors, moving photocatalyst design from empirical tuning toward a predictive, function‐aware paradigm.

title: Halogen‐Dependent Regulation of the Thyroid Hormone Transporter by Antipsychotic Drugs and Their Analogues
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Antipsychotic drugs are primarily used to manage psychosis and other psychotic disorders. Their main mechanism of action involves blocking dopamine D2 receptors in the brain, and they remain important for the treatment for schizophrenia. In this paper, we describe an unusual property of several commonly used antipsychotic drugs and their analogues for their ability to modulate the thyroid hormone transporter system. Specifically, these compounds significantly increase the protein expression of monocarboxylate transporter 8 (MCT8), a key transporter responsible for carrying thyroid hormones across the plasma membrane in a variety of cell lines. Our findings indicate that the presence of halogen substituents plays a critical role in promoting the MCT8 upregulation. Furthermore, the magnitude of this effect is dependent on the nature of the halogen atom, with iodine‐containing phenothiazine derivatives exhibiting the strongest induction of MCT8 expression. The increased transporter expression was accompanied by enhanced cellular uptake of MCT8‐selective fluorescent probes, confirming functional activity. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first example of halogen‐dependent regulation of protein expression in mammalian cells.

title: Cascade Radical Homopolymerization of Isocyanide‐Containing Monomers via Photoinitiation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Isocyanides are highly valuable building blocks in organic synthesis and have been established as
                    C1

Although their radical copolymerization with electron‐deficient partners such as acrylates has been reported, the long‐standing challenge of radical homopolymerization remains unresolved. Herein, we report the first successful radical cascade homopolymerization of isocyanide monomers. This strategy is enabled by a novel monomer design that promotes a sequence of radical translocation and ring closure over fragmentation. The process efficiently affords polymers featuring an unprecedented backbone of five‐membered cyclic imines. Moreover, the use of phenyl isocyanide enables the direct synthesis of polyindoles. This work introduces a versatile platform for increasing architectural complexity in polymer backbones and opens new avenues for monomer design in radical polymerization.

title: Entropy‐Triggered Mechanistic Reconfiguration: Unleashing Adjacent‐Site Oxygen Coupling to Circumvent Scaling Limit in Water Oxidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains the anodic bottleneck of water electrolysis for green hydrogen production. The conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) is constrained by linear scaling relationships, whereas lattice oxygen involvement inevitably causes structural degradation, imposing a persistent activity‐stability trade‐off. Here, we realize a mechanistic transition from AEM to the oxide pathway mechanism (OPM), thereby circumventing the activity scaling limit, by constructing a noble‐metal‐free high‐entropy spinel oxide featuring a three‐dimensionally ordered macroporous (3DOM) hierarchical porous architecture. Mn/Al‐induced high‐entropy lattice contraction shortens adjacent‐metal distances, providing the geometric prerequisite for direct O–O coupling. Meanwhile, entropy‐driven electronic redistribution elevates Co valence and modulates Co–O covalency, optimizing oxygenated‐intermediate adsorption and enriching surface *OH species for subsequent O–O coupling. The 3DOM hierarchical porous framework further exposes OPM‐favorable sites and accelerates mass transport. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a low overpotential of 218 mV at 10 mA cm
                    −2
                    , sustains stable operation for over 3000 h at 100 mA cm
                    −2
                    , and enables an anion‐exchange membrane water electrolyzer to achieve 1.604 V at 1 A cm
                    −2
                    with 2500 h durability. This mechanism‐guided high‐entropy design opens a route beyond the activity‐stability trade‐off.

title: Electric‐Field Responsive Molecular Switch Unlocks Stable 4.5 V‐Class Sodium Layered Oxide Cathodes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  High‐voltage operation of sodium layered oxide cathodes is essential for unlocking energy density, yet the intensified interfacial electric field destabilizes the cathode/electrolyte interphase (CEI), posing a persistent challenge. Herein, we reveal that interfacial stability is governed not solely by oxidative tolerance but by the coupling of molecular species to the dynamically evolving interfacial field. Guided by this insight, we define an electric field coupling agent (EFCA) that combines strong field responsiveness with appropriate redox propensity to enable threshold‐gated reactivity. Acting as a molecular switch, the agent remains chemically inactive below a critical field but becomes activated above it through field‐driven migration, reorientation, and selective bond cleavage. A dual‐descriptor framework integrating a customized field sensitivity index (FSI) with HOMO energy identifies sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate as an effective switch. Upon activation, the resulting field‐insensitive and electrochemically inert fragments assemble into a self‐limiting and compositionally gradient interphase with a boron‐rich outer layer. Such coupled interfacial chemistry achieves a counterintuitive field‐enhanced stability, enabling the manganese‐based sodium layered cathode to cycle stably at 4.5 V with 87.9% retention after 1000 cycles and demonstrating practical viability in 1 Ah pouch cells. The mechanism is further validated across analogous layered oxides, establishing a generalizable paradigm for on‐demand interfacial protection in high‐voltage batteries.

abstract: New catalytic manifolds that challenge existing boundaries for synthesis and sustainable manufacturing are notoriously difficult to implement1, particularly for catalytic paradigms based on metals which lack access to the fundamental processes that underpin many established d-block mechanistic pathways (e.g. oxidative addition and reductive elimination). The widespread exploitation of systems based on main-group elements therefore requires alternative elementary steps to effect turnover. Herein, we demonstrate a new catalytic platform for nucleophilic fluorination, which exploits a complex based on calcium (the fifth most Earth-abundant element) as the fluoride delivery vehicle. The key intermediate is a calcium-fluoride complex featuring a terminal Ca–F interaction, a unique structural geometry enabled by a highly sterically encumbered dianionic ligand-scaffold. This intermediate links reactants and products through F– capture and release steps, and thereby unlocks catalytic F– shuttling. Late Ca–F bond breaking in the rate-determining fluoride-delivery transition-state means that electronic and steric tuning of F– by calcium is chemically significant; proof-of-concept results show a hitherto unprecedented level of selectivity for substitution over elimination brought about by Ca-modulation. In a broader context, this work demonstrates how control over catalyst speciation and reagent binding affinity are key factors for the future development of sustainable non-transition metal paradigms in catalysis.

title: The retention of nanoparticles in solid tumours
abstract: The active transport and retention principle states that nanoparticles enter tumours via endothelial cells and exit via lymphatic drainage. How nanoparticles are retained in the tumour microenvironment remains unclear. Here we report a computational strategy to determine the mechanism of nanoparticle retention in solid tumours. We find that tumour cellular and acellular components delay and obstruct the movement of nanoparticles by influencing nanoparticle drag, Brownian and electric forces. We mathematically define nanoparticle retention based on these interactions, linking retention quantitatively to tumour pathophysiology, nanoparticle design and delivery efficiency. We create a software interface to simulate and predict nanoparticle retention across different tumour systems and nanoparticle designs, enabling us to select optimal tumour and nanoparticle delivery conditions for better therapeutic outcomes.

abstract: Hydrous carbonaceous chondrites are potential carriers of exogenous water to the Earth–Moon system, yet well-preserved hydrous carbonaceous impactor fragments are rarely found in lunar samples, with previous discoveries limited to the lunar nearside. The Chang’e-6 mission returned the first sample from the farside, providing a unique opportunity to identify the exogenous materials that have added volatiles to this region. We document well‑preserved relics showing C1-like mineralogical features in a Chang’e-6 regolith breccia. They are dominated by fine-grained Mg-rich saponite with partially collapsed basal spacing, along with magnetite, dolomite, sulfides, and organic nanoglobules, matching mineral assemblages of heavily altered carbonaceous chondrites and hydrous materials returned from asteroids Ryugu and Bennu. This diagnostic mineral assemblage and in‑situ space‑weathering overprint confirm that these clasts are surviving fragments of the incoming impactor, and in situ dehydration records water loss during lunar surface exposure. Our study provides the first mineralogical and petrographic evidence for preserved hydrous carbonaceous impact debris in lunar farside regolith, revealing the microscale preservation of hydrated minerals and carbonaceous components and providing new constraints on impact-induced volatile injection and release from carbonaceous materials.

Exploring the distributional implications of targeted residential electrification in California
abstract: Residential electrification can reduce emissions but its household economics remain uncertain in regions with high electricity prices. Here we report a household-level analysis of 21,609 gas-heated homes in California, evaluating costs, emissions and equity under alternative end-use, tariff and rollout scenarios. Across modelled scenarios, only 15% of households achieve positive net present values. Cost-effectiveness is substantially higher for homes with existing air conditioning: 53–72% break even when electrifying space heating, compared with fewer than 10% of homes without it. Lower-volumetric tariffs improve bill savings under full electrification for many households, although outcomes vary by assistance-programme enrolment. Modelled income-targeted rebates substantially improve outcomes for low- and moderate-income households. Targeting areas with older gas infrastructure yields emissions reductions comparable to higher-income-first adoption but a larger aggregate private net present value shortfall. Lower installation costs, targeted incentives and tariff reform are therefore central to equitable, widespread residential electrification across high-cost electricity regions.

abstract: The reduction propensity of the electrolyte governs the interfacial stability of batteries. By examining solvation participation and electron-acquisition propensity, this work establishes a preorganized interphasial reduction principle that quantifies molecular reduction propensity. Leveraging this principle, we screened 72 molecules and identified CMDO as the effective additive capable of suppressing the side reactions of ethyl acetate at the interface.

abstract: An amphiphilic ionic bicontinuous mesoporous carbon nitride enables simultaneous photocatalytic co-production of H2O2 and tandem C–H activation/C–N cyclization at the oil-water interface. By repurposing a sacrificial agent into a high-value pharmaceutical intermediate (BzlM), this dual-functional catalyst sustains co-production in a continuous-flow reactor for over 200 hours, offering a generalizable strategy for sustainable biphasic chemical synthesis.

abstract: Reducing iridium use without sacrificing activity and durability is a key challenge for proton-exchange membrane water electrolysis. By linking Ir electronic state to catalyst stability, this study offers a general strategy for designing low-Ir, durable anodes for practical green hydrogen production.

Stepwise Proximity Labeling With a Switchable Organophotocatalyst
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photoinducible proximity labeling (PL) using photocatalysts offers high spatiotemporal resolution for profiling protein–protein interactions (PPIs). Conventional approaches require genetic installation of a tag to tether the photocatalyst to a protein of interest (POI), which may perturb native protein function and cause artificial labeling. Ligand‐directed delivery of photocatalysts to native POIs has emerged as a tag‐free alternative; however, this strategy suffers from nonspecific labeling by unbound catalysts and an inherent washing dilemma, where insufficient washing leads to background labeling while excessive washing disrupts ligand binding. These limitations have severely restricted tag‐free and ligand‐directed PPI profiling. Herein, we report a switchable photoinducible PL strategy based on a nitrobenzoxadiazole (NBD) unit that becomes catalytically active only after covalent conjugation to a POI. This approach consists of a two‐step process: introduction of an
                    N
                    ‐NBD moiety into the POI using a catalytically inactive
                    O
                    ‐NBD unit, followed by light‐induced PL catalyzed by
                    N
                    ‐NBD.
                    N
                    ‐methyl luminol and 1‐methyl‐4‐arylurazole were identified as labeling reagents selectively activated by
                    N
                    ‐NBD. Targeting mitochondrial voltage‐dependent anion channel (VDAC) enabled selective labeling and proteomic identification of mitochondrial proteins. This switchable PL method circumvents the washing dilemma, suppresses nonspecific labeling, and enables tag‐free proteomic analysis with improved spatial selectivity.

title: Anodic Selective Etching: A Mechanism‐Centric Perspective for Electrochemical Subtractive Manufacturing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Anodic selective etching (ASE) is a precision electrochemical subtractive manufacturing strategy that enables controllable material removal, interfacial reconstruction, and morphology evolution under electrochemically controlled conditions. Unlike material‐centric reviews that mainly catalogue substrates or products, this mechanism‐centric framework reveals common electrochemical principles, enabling cross‐material comparison, transferable design rules, and predictive control over selectivity, reaction location, and structural evolution. This review unifies ASE across material platforms and structural scales through five dominant modes: composition‐ and phase‐selective anodic dissolution, structural site‐selective anodic etching, semiconductor carrier‐ and space‐charge‐controlled etching, film‐ and passivation‐controlled subtraction, and geometry‐ or three‐phase boundary‐localized etching, together with representative coupled mechanisms. The roles of anodic material characteristics, electrolyte composition, and electrochemical parameters in defining selectivity windows, localization behavior, and structural outcomes are critically discussed. These mechanisms enable low‐dimensional materials, porous and core–shell architectures, surface finishing and shaping, and meniscus‐localized tip fabrication. Key challenges in multicomponent selectivity, electrolyte sustainability, and scalable manufacturing are outlined, alongside opportunities in in situ and operando characterization, multi‐physics modeling, and data‐driven optimization toward reproducible and programmable electrochemical manufacturing.

title: Metallurgical Interface Engineering Constructing In Situ Li3N‐Enriched Interphase: A Bulk‐Interface Synergy Strategy Toward Practical Silicon Anodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Silicon anodes are promising for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries but suffer from volume expansion, unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and sluggish Li
                    +
                    diffusion. Herein, we report a vacuum‐suspension‐melted (VSM) bulk multiphase integration and interphase modification strategy to address these challenges. Unlike conventional mechanical mixing, VSM constructs a SiSnM (M = Bi, Ni) composite with metallurgically bonded Si/metal interfaces, forming a conductive network that buffers internal stress via atomic‐scale interfacial stress transfer. Simultaneously, a polydopamine‐derived nitrogen‐doped carbon coating transforms in situ into a Li
                    3
                    N‐enriched interphase during cycling, which exhibits high ionic/electronic conductivity, accelerates interfacial charge transfer, and suppresses continuous SEI breakdown. The resulting SiSnM@Li
                    3
                    N anode delivers 87.3% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 1.5 A g
                    −1
                    and >1000 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 15 A g
                    −1
                    , with reliable operation from −30°C to 60°C. Stable cycling at 2.5 mg cm
                    −2
                    confirms practical relevance. Full cells with Li‐rich Mn‐based cathodes show stable performance, and 5 Ah‐level pouch cells deliver 84.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 6 A discharge. This work concurrently tackles ionic, electronic, and mechanical constraints, offering a practical path to high‐energy durable Si‐based batteries.

title: Acoustic‐Electromagnetic Information Sensing and Security Protection via Intelligent Transparency Metasurfaces
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Acoustic‐electromagnetic (EM) cross‐domain sensing converts information carried by sound‐induced mechanical vibrations into remotely measurable EM signals, supporting applications in human–computer interaction, environmental sensing, and the Internet of Things. However, the ability to reconstruct acoustic information from weak phase signatures in EM echoes also creates a risk of acoustic information leakage. Existing shielding and encryption schemes are difficult to combine with covert integration and real‐time reconfigurability, and struggle to intervene directly in the mapping process, thereby are poorly suited to end‐to‐end threats in complex scenarios. Here, we propose an interface for cross‐domain sensing and security protection based on an optically transparent intelligent metasurface with reconfigurable control over echo amplitude and phase. The intelligent metasurface reshapes the acoustic‐to‐EM mapping and controls the demodulated output without altering the acoustic source signal. We fabricate a prototype with programmable amplitude and phase control and partial optical transparency. Experiments demonstrate three controllable effects along the acoustic–EM transduction chain: acoustic information suppression, ambiguity generation, and hallucinatory speech output in the absence of acoustic excitation. This work provides an integrable and configurable physical‐layer paradigm for cross‐domain protection and information manipulation in cross‐domain sensing systems.

title: Reaction‐Induced Dynamic Covalent Networking Enables Adaptive Vesicles and Hierarchical Biointerfaces
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Conventional vesicular assemblies often face challenges in balancing mechanical robustness with structural adaptability. Here, we develop a reaction‐induced dynamic covalent networking (RIDCN) strategy that integrates vesicle construction with adaptive biointerface engineering. Through the formation of interconnected imine and boronate ester linkages, RIDCN directs the assembly of non‐amphiphilic building blocks into vesicular structures, with dynamic covalent networks serving as integral membrane frameworks. This structural integration reinforces vesicle mechanics while preserving adaptive reorganization through reversible bond exchange. Beyond individual vesicles, RIDCN enables interfacial assembly on diverse implant substrates, forming adaptive coatings with antibacterial, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and osteogenic activities. These findings demonstrate the potential of RIDCN to connect vesicle construction, mechanical adaptation, and multifunctional biointerface engineering within a unified material design strategy.

title: The scientific record is never finished
abstract:
The scholarly scientific record has always been a work in progress. From the earliest days of scientific publishing, new findings would come along that changed the way earlier findings are understood. When research journals were published only in print, occasional errors would be reported by the authors or found by others, and papers would be retracted or corrected. When publishing became digital, many more people could quickly access and scrutinize data and images for accuracy. Now, in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), it is possible for machines to do these examinations more expeditiously and at a larger scale. All of this has added an important new layer to the publishing process and put more responsibility on authors, who must update their work if new issues arise. In response to this need,
                    Science
                    is improving the ways in which it will flag and notate papers that require adjustment or where changes are under consideration. Our Editorial Policies now reflect these updates.

title: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress
abstract: Childhood adversity increases the risk of chronic pain and anxiety later in life, particularly in women, yet the neural mechanisms linking early-life stress to adult vulnerability remain elusive. Here, we show that social isolation and nerve injury interact to amplify activity-dependent synaptic gain and anticipatory recruitment of the paraventricular thalamus-to–central amygdala pathway in female, but not male, mice. This female-specific circuit sensitization enhances mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance behaviors in adulthood. Chemogenetic pathway inhibition selectively rescued these behaviors when stress and injury co-occurred, whereas sustained and phasic pathway activation triggered mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance, respectively. Together, these findings uncovered a latent thalamo-amygdalar synaptic gain state that is unmasked by a subsequent injury and transforms early-life stress into female-specific vulnerability to chronic pain and anxiety-like avoidance.

title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
abstract: Turbulence is chaotic, yet its fluctuations follow a structured, nonequilibrium energy cascade unconstrained by the equilibrium theorems that limit passive energy extraction from molecular gases. Here, we introduce turbulence shelters: hollow shells with a single aperture that filter eddies by scale, sustaining gradients in fluctuation intensity that drive directional particle transport despite zero mean fluid flux. Across three orders of magnitude in size, shelters establish particle concentration contrasts between their interior and the surrounding flow, with selectivity controlled by particle geometry, inertia, thermal fluctuations, and electrostatic forces. At the microscale, shelters discriminate particles differing by tens of nanometers independently of material composition. These results establish a design principle for selective filtration: Geometry that compartmentalizes turbulent fluctuations can harness ambient eddies to direct particle transport.

title: Beyond containment in insect farming
Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
abstract:
Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year
                    −1
                    ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year
                    −1
                    (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year
                    −1
                    (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

title: Angular momentum transfer from an optical vortex to an atomic rotor
abstract:
Light carries angular momentum in two forms: spin, associated with polarization, and orbital, associated with helical wavefronts. Whereas spin angular momentum underlies well-known atomic selection rules, the role of orbital angular momentum (OAM) in light-matter interaction continues to be discussed in the literature. In this work, we investigate OAM transfer from a vortex laser beam to a trapped-ion quantum rotor using rotational sidebands of the electric quadrupole transition of
                    40
                    Ca
                    +
                    . We directly observe coherent transfer of optical OAM into quantized rotation and identify distinct selection rules for different rotational sidebands. This observation provides experimental evidence for a scale-dependent separation of angular momentum transfer pathways in light-matter interactions. Further, our work elucidates the previously reported modified selection rules in trapped-ion experiments, establishing a unified framework for twisted light–matter interactions.

title: Meso–microporous zeolitic materials with thin walls containing ordered 10-ring channels
abstract: Aluminosilicate zeolites offer exceptional size and shape selectivity but suffer from diffusion limitations imposed by subnanometer micropores. Intrinsically meso–microporous zeolites integrate mesopores with micropores to create interconnected pathways that accelerate diffusion while preserving selectivity, yet their synthesis remains challenging. In this study, we report NJU120-5 and NJU120-7, intrinsically meso–microporous aluminosilicates that integrate micropores with mesopores enclosed by two-T-atom-thick walls containing 10-ring channels, forming a fully interconnected three-dimensional pore network. Their plausible framework models were established on the basis of advanced electron ptychographic imaging, revealing representative quasi-rectangular mesopores in calcined NJU120-5 with a uniform width of ~12 angstroms and lengths from 41 to 162 angstroms. Both materials exhibit high porosity, strong Brønsted acidity, and enhanced performance in heavy-oil cracking, delivering high yields of valuable fuels with suppressed coke formation.

title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
abstract:
Quantum phenomena can be exploited to tackle certain problems beyond the reach of classical approaches. In this study, we focus on coordinated decision-making among many players without communication, the study of which, on current quantum processors, has remained elusive. Using a superconducting qubit processor, we show that quantum contextuality enables certain tasks to be performed with success probabilities beyond classical limits. With a few qubits, we illustrate quantum contextuality with the magic square game and quantify it through a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality violation. To examine many-body contextuality, we implement the
                    N
                    -player Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger game and separately solve a two-dimensional hidden linear function problem, advancing the state of the art on fidelity and system size in both tasks. Our work introduces benchmarking of quantum processors using contextuality-based algorithms.

title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis
abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces
abstract: Ultrasound imaging relies on soft interfaces that transmit sound efficiently between a device and the body. Conventional gel couplants provide low acoustic loss but contain mobile liquid phases that can dry, flow, or leach during extended use. By contrast, mobile phase–free elastomers are more stable but generally attenuate megahertz ultrasound strongly, limiting their use as couplants. We report an interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer molecularly designed to overcome this trade-off. A densely grafted backbone lowers the shear modulus without increasing shear loss, whereas well-packed sidechains reduce bulk compressibility, jointly suppressing acoustic attenuation in a soft elastomer. The resulting elastomer combines soft tissue–like mechanics with low-loss acoustics, providing a durable couplant for soft ultrasonic interfaces.

Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling
abstract: Real-time monitoring of chemical reactions is often achieved with specialized instrumentation along with custom-designed reactors or intrusive sampling. In this study, we introduce reaction telemetry, a wireless analytical strategy that enables remote, nonintrusive monitoring directly within operating reaction vessels. This approach uses light-powered microelectronic devices that communicate optically and function as autonomous sensing elements. We demonstrate continuous calorimetric measurements across diverse chemical reactions relevant to pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, including photochemical and electrochemical systems, providing access to reaction kinetics under native operating conditions with subsecond temporal resolution. The resulting measurements will support catalyst evaluation, safety assessment, and mechanistic investigation and will accelerate data-driven reaction discovery. By embedding analytical functionality directly within reaction vessels, reaction telemetry establishes a general framework for information-rich observation of chemical processes across research, development, and education.
